title: Training Without Fooling Yourself: The Step Size, a Network That Learns the Noise, and Stopping on a Validation Set

questions.question: Why is the training error the wrong thing to judge a network by?
options: It is always zero
It is too noisy to read
It goes on falling while the network learns the noise of its training set
It is measured in the wrong units
questions.explanation: A network with enough weights can fit its training samples, noise and all. Only data it has not seen says whether it learned the task.

questions.question: With a step of 1.0, what happened to the weights?
options: They grew without bound and the error became NaN
They stayed where they started
They reached the best error fastest
They learned the noise
questions.explanation: Each step overshot the minimum by more than the last. A NaN in training is nearly always a step that is too large.

questions.question: On 30 noisy samples, where was the validation error lowest and where did it end?
options: Lowest at the last epoch, 0.0448
0.0280 at epoch 346, and 0.0448 at the end
0.00012 at the end
It fell all the way, like the training error
questions.explanation: After epoch 346 the network fitted the noise of its 30 samples, and the validation error rose.

questions.question: Training stopped with a patience of 200. At which epoch, and whose weights did it keep?
options: At epoch 3000, keeping the last weights
At epoch 346, keeping the last weights
At epoch 200, keeping the first weights
At epoch 546, keeping the weights of epoch 346
questions.explanation: It went on for 200 epochs without improvement, then gave back the best weights it had seen.

questions.question: Why are the samples shuffled from a seed each epoch?
options: So each episode does not pull the network in turn, and so the run can be repeated exactly
Because the gradient is wrong otherwise
To make training faster per step
To hide which samples are in the test set
questions.explanation: Shuffling breaks the order of the episodes; the seed makes the shuffle, and so the weights, the same every time.

questions.question: Which set should the stopping epoch be chosen on?
options: The test set, since that is what is reported
The training set
A validation set kept apart from both
Whichever set gives the lowest number
questions.explanation: Choosing on the test set makes it part of training. The test set is looked at once, at the end.
